## **Meeting Sep 24, 2026 at 19:45 BST**

Meeting records [Transcript](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1z6E7Jwy2-pqWl_LSg9R2CuaS76BsGObSm2U2V_PzDQM/edit?usp=drive_web&tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a) 

### **Summary**

Website prototype review with feature feedback and navigation analysis

**Website Navigation and Filtering**  
Prototype walkthrough highlighted user preferences for filtering personal computer parts by metrics and deals.

**Component Specifications and Design**  
Review of build pages led to requests for clear compatibility indicators and visible hardware specifications.

**Resources and Workspace Guides**  
Discussion on educational resources suggested expanding workspace preparation sections with instructional videos.

### **Next steps**

- [ ] \[Jay D\] Update Part Filters: Update the filtering and addition logic for website components to better facilitate user browsing and selection.

- [ ] \[Jay D\] Resolve Loading Issues: Improve website loading times and resolve server connectivity errors encountered during the demonstration.

- [ ] \[Jay D\] Follow Up: Send a message to the meeting participant with an update on the project outcome following the presentation.

### **Details**

* **Website Navigation and CPU Filtering**: Jay D walked Abd ElRahman Mohamed Hassan Abdou M Soliman through a prototype personal computer building website designed to let users browse parts, create builds, and purchase components via third-party websites. When asked how they would search for a central processing unit, Abd ElRahman Mohamed Hassan Abdou M Soliman stated they would click on "browse parts" and use the left-hand category filters, noting that brand preferences and socket types are less important than finding the best deal and filtering by metrics like cores and central processing unit speed ([00:01:54](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.wmy8spo15hzr)).

  ![][image1]

* **Component List and Wattage Tracking**: Abd ElRahman Mohamed Hassan Abdou M Soliman reviewed the process for viewing added parts, stating they would want to see a list displaying individual wattages and a summary of total wattage ([00:02:47](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.8i0rgz20xsww)). Jay D removed the basket icon from the top right corner because users do not check out directly on the platform, which surprised Abd ElRahman Mohamed Hassan Abdou M Soliman, who expected a basket there rather than a "my build" link in the middle ([00:04:11](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.7wmx6dnty4b1)). Upon viewing the "my build" page, Abd ElRahman Mohamed Hassan Abdou M Soliman noted it displayed an estimated wattage of 250 watts alongside socket types, form factors, storage, and memory specifications, but requested a clear compatibility indicator or checkbox for each item without needing to click into them ([00:04:59](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.3lgu1ed96e50)).

  ![][image2]

* **Component Specification Preferences**: Abd ElRahman Mohamed Hassan Abdou M Soliman detailed specific component information they want visible while making decisions. For central processing units, they want to see core counts and speeds; for random-access memory, they look for types like DDR4 or DDR5 and speed configurations. For graphics processing units, Abd ElRahman Mohamed Hassan Abdou M Soliman noted that users rely more on model numbers, prices, and benchmarks than deep specifications ([00:06:55](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.6lmx2b6vmiwl)). For storage, they want to immediately identify whether a drive is a hard drive, solid-state drive, SATA, NVMe, or M.2, along with the form factor. For power supplies, they prioritize physical size and whether the cables are fixed or removable ([00:07:46](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.28ipq44g5kqd)).

* **Homepage Design and Terminology**: Abd ElRahman Mohamed Hassan Abdou M Soliman reviewed the homepage and suggested removing the "browse by category" section at the bottom, arguing that users do not use a personal computer parts matcher to search for single components. They recommended replacing the "browse parts" label with a more engaging call to action such as "build your PC" ([00:08:45](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.5r57pzro1cbb)). During the walkthrough, Jay D displayed a metric showing 50k builders on the platform ([00:09:41](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.51064cwrgmj2)).

  ![][image3]

* **Resources, Guides, and Workspace Preparation**: Jay D presented the site's compatibility guide and frequently asked questions section, noting it is designed for users with little computer knowledge ([00:09:41](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.51064cwrgmj2)) ([00:11:59](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.qlajofjbje41)). Abd ElRahman Mohamed Hassan Abdou M Soliman recommended expanding the workspace preparation section to include equipment recommendations and purchase links for items like anti-static wristbands using platforms like Amazon or Newegg ([00:10:47](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.ir52zj41qwah)). Furthermore, Abd ElRahman Mohamed Hassan Abdou M Soliman suggested incorporating instructional videos and useful visual resources to better support visual learners ([00:11:59](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.qlajofjbje41)), a suggestion Jay D acknowledged as beneficial ([00:12:54](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.njhhw92gbuv6)).

  ![][image4]

* **Research Wrap-Up and Next Steps**: Jay D apologized for initial service loading delays at the beginning of the session ([00:12:54](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.njhhw92gbuv6)). Jay D explained that this meeting served as research utilizing the transcript feature for the first time, and the gathered feedback will be discussed in their upcoming presentation or used to detail alternative design implementations. Jay D thanked Abd ElRahman Mohamed Hassan Abdou M Soliman for their time, and Abd ElRahman Mohamed Hassan Abdou M Soliman offered to participate in future calls if additional feedback is required ([00:13:30](?tab=t.j72mp0ccy25a#heading=h.e5yul27bd99e)).
